newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SEEN UP ON HIGHER INFLATION.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SEEN UP ON HIGHER INFLATION.

text.p: Trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market are expected to harden this month on the back of higher consumer inflation data for September, dealers said on Wednesday.
Figures released by the central Reserve Bank on Wednesday show September consumer inflation rising to 20.6 percent year-on-year from 17.7 percent in August.
"We expect the rates to be on an upward trend following the inflation figure," one dealer said.
Money market rates have this year fallen from around 30 percent at the beginning of the year to the lower 20s.
Another dealer said a cut to 27 percent from 27.5 percent in the Reserve Bank's rediscount rate, also announced on Wednesday, would not have much effect on the money market rates.
"The rediscount rate cut will just affect the minimum lending rates of commercial banks. They will feel obliged to reduce their minimum lending rates," he added.
On the money market on Wednesday, the dealers said the market was short of about Z$55 million following mid-month statutory reserve payments by some banks and rates were mixed to firmer.
Dealers, however, said they expected the shortage to ease later due to maturing treasury bills.
The rates for NCDs with maturities of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 22 percent and sold at 21.5 percent compared to 22.5 percent and 21.5 percent on Tuesday.

Bankers' acceptance bills were being bought at 21.5 percent and sold at 21 percent versus 21.5 percent and 20.15 percent while the call rate was flactuating between 15 and 20 percent compared to 18 percent.
